title: Getting her song back from Bess Berman after Mahalia Jackson recorded it
summary: Apollo's Bess Berman put out Mahalia's version of Hunter's song under a changed title; Mahalia announced the true author at a Brooklyn concert and Hunter got her song back.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: now, didn't you also write some songs for Mahalia Jackson?

Yeah. What's -- I got that record. I got some of those records too. What was her first one? You see, I wrote a song called, 'Will The Day Ever Come When I Can Rest,' and I took it down to Bess Berman, who owned the record company at the time.

Yes, Apollo, and asked her if she would ask Mahalia to do it. I didn't know Mahalia very well at the time, see. So she said, well, I don't know, you know. She don't know she's working -- I was as smart as she was. I don't know, but you leave it here. So I did.

And anyhow, Mahalia recorded it. It was a good song. One day Doc Wheeler and I were talking. I was at Doc Wheeler's house to see his wife, Judy, and he says, girl, Mahalia just made a record that's out of this world. I say, yes? Said, yes.

He says -- I say what's the name of it. He said, 'I Wonder If I Will Ever Rest.' This woman had changed the title. 'I Wonder If I will Ever Rest.' So he said that -- it was right around the corner there was a record store, and he said, the woman right around the corner from here, she has a record of it. And I said, oh, I certainly would like to hear
it. So he said, come on, let's go get it. And I went and got it. It was my song.

I didn't say a word until it made some money. And then I went to -- to the publisher who published it and I -- I think -- let me see who had it. Anyhow I spoke about it, and I spoke to AGAC, you know, my society. And they got -- they asked her about the song, and she said it wasn't mine. It was Mahalia's. She kept on denying it and did everything she could, until one Sunday somebody told me Mahalia was giving a concert in Brooklyn.

Now, I don't know what Mahalia was going to do because I hadn't seen her to talk to her, and when I -- during this concert -- now, this woman and all her friends, this woman -- her record -- the Apollo record company, was sitting in the audience. And I'm sitting there.

Mahalia says, my next song, ladies and gentlemen, was written by a good friend of mine, and I want you to hear it. And she sang that song. She says, written by this lady sitting right here, Alberta Hunter, a good friend of mine, and when she said that, what could Bess Berman do?

So she had to give me my song back, and it came all out in the newspapers, and I think I have that, where I got my song back. She had just changed the title, but the song was written -- you'd lose the sense of it if you try

See? So I got my song back. And let me see. What's the other one? Not-Thank You, Lord. I'll have to look at my list because so many -- I've had so many people record so many good songs -- so many -- good people record them, you know.
